glance.question: Is mental illness a spiritual problem, a medical one, or both, and who should treat it?

positions.name: Biblical Counseling
positions.claim: Scripture is sufficient for counseling; secular psychology adds nothing essential.

positions.name: Christian Integration
positions.claim: Scripture leads, with psychology and medicine serving as tools of care.

positions.name: Medical Realism
positions.claim: Mental illness is real illness; therapy and medication need no apology.

start_here.title: The Heart of Depression
start_here.author: Edward Welch
start_here.why: Names five possible causes of depression and urges helpers to treat it first as suffering.

start_here.title: Scrambling for the Light: Christian Depression and the Use of Medication
start_here.author: Kathryn Butler
start_here.why: A physician argues that antidepressants can be received as one of God's gifts of common kindness.

start_here.title: The Anxious Church
start_here.author: J. D. Peabody
start_here.why: A pastor who lives with anxiety and OCD asks why churches grow uneasy around unresolved pain.

key_number.text: 26% of churchgoers say their church encourages medication for mental illness; 54% say it encourages counseling.
key_number.study: Suicide and the Church Research Study
